name: Why is a waterproofing membrane necessary before setting shower tile?

mainEntity.name: Why is a waterproofing membrane necessary before setting shower tile?

acceptedAnswer.text: Waterproofing must happen behind the tile because tile and grout joints are not completely waterproof on their own. Water vapor and moisture seep through grout lines over time, which can rot standard drywall and framing studs if the substrate is untreated. Professional shower installation requires moisture-resistant backer board, taped seams, and a continuous liquid or sheet waterproofing membrane across all wet areas. Neglecting this crucial step often leads to hidden mold growth, cracked tiles, and structural floor damage that eventually requires a complete tear-out to fix.
acceptedAnswer.description: Tile and grout are naturally porous, so a sealed waterproof backer system behind them is essential to prevent moisture damage, rot, and mold inside wall cavities.
